ledger.claim: The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is met. EV-TRIP-00106, EV-GPS-00106 and EV-FARE-00106 all carry trip_id TRP-00106 and agree on the booking, and the trace covers the whole trip from the 08:35:15 start to the 09:03:15 end at 100% coverage with no gaps, so the artifacts describe the same trip.

The route deviation is ESTABLISHED under POL-RD-01 on the governing trace figure. The trace measures 10.78 km against a booked optimal of 7.2 km — an excess of 3.58 km, which is 49.72% of optimal. Both limbs pass: the excess exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms and exceeds 20% of optimal. The trip_record's rounded 10.8 km convenience copy may NOT be cited for this threshold test.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It carries 169 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds — nowhere near the 90-second gap, 500 m jump or 30-second sampling-interval limbs. The deviation therefore stands on the trace alone and needs no independent corroboration.

The fare evidence independently confirms the vehicle was on the CTE corridor the optimal Thomson Road route never uses. The fare_breakdown marks both charged gantries — 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)' at 08:41:22 and 'CTE (Chin Swee Rd tunnel, towards City)' at 08:50:51 — as on_optimal_route false, and the trace passes each of them (nearest fixes 0.0 m and 24.1 m).

The rider's contemporaneous in-app message corroborates the detour: at 08:46:30, well before the 09:03:15 drop-off, the rider wrote 'why we at havelock? bugis is behind us' — placing the vehicle west of the Bugis destination on the CTE corridor, consistent with the trace and inconsistent with the direct Thomson Road route.

Nothing exonerates the excess under POL-RD-03. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00106-01, is MISSING — it carries no payload and weight 0.0 — so no advisory names any road the optimal route traverses and no closure can be asserted. The absence is itself citable, and the whole established excess flows to POL-RD-02.

The detour was not rider-requested, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable. The chat log holds a single rider message sent at 08:46:30 — after the vehicle had already left the optimal corridor — and it is a complaint, not an instruction; waypoint_hint is null and no road is named. With nothing to corroborate, the clause's waypoint test cannot be run and no distance is excluded from excess.

With no exculpatory clause surviving and fare_model METERED, the POL-RD-02 recomputation runs: (3.80 + 0.75 x 7.2 + 0.28 x 19.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP on the optimal route + 0 fixed surcharges = 15.32. Charged total is 26.04, so the refund is 26.04 - 15.32 = 10.72, rounded up to SGD 10.75. That is a PARTIAL_REFUND for the filing rider, comfortably above the 0.50 de minimis floor.

The 5.50 of ERP is not lost to the rider, but it is also not added on top. Because the recomputed fare includes only on-optimal-route gantries and the optimal route carries zero ERP, the two off-route gantries (3.00 + 2.50) are already comprehended in the 10.75 refund and must be itemised for transparency only, per POL-RD-09(1).

No extra corroboration burden attaches to the rider. The POL-RD-08 rider-profile trigger requires deviation_claims_60d of 4 or more with 1 or fewer substantiated; the rider stands at 1 and 1. These are the only rider_profile fields POL-GEN-01 permits to be cited for this test, and they do not cut against the claim.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so this case can be ruled rather than escalated. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired and complete; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing or non-covering artifact; the refund of 10.75 is far below the 150.00 ceiling; and both charged gantries are matched to the trace.

I do not press a full refund, and I say so plainly rather than stretch the record. The excess of 49.72% falls just below the 50% MATERIAL threshold, so no material deviation is recorded; and even if the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check were engaged, deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 96 completed trips, so no repeat pattern exists and the POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift is unavailable on these figures.

The governing GPS trace measures 10.78 km against a booked optimal of 7.2 km — an excess of 3.58 km, or 49.72% of optimal. That clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (over 20% and over 0.8 km absolute, both of which must pass) but it sits BELOW the 50%-of-optimal figure and far below the 8.0 km figure that POL-RD-01 makes the additional MATERIALITY test. This is an ordinary, non-material deviation: the mandatory driver_profile check under POL-RD-06 is not engaged on this trip, and neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor the driver-conduct referral that clause licenses can follow from it.

The trip_record's rounded actual_distance_km of 10.8 km would compute to exactly 50.0% and straddle the materiality line, but POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the GOVERNING measurement and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. Measured the way the clause requires — trace distance 10.78 km less optimal 7.2 km = 3.58 km excess, 49.72% — the deviation falls below materiality. The rider's case therefore cannot be escalated into a material-deviation finding on the rounded convenience copy.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be established under POL-RD-06. The driver has 0 deviation flags in the trailing 90 days across 96 completed trips. Neither limb of the pattern test fires: 0 is below the 3-flag threshold, and 0/96 is below the 0.05 ratio (which in any event requires at least 40 completed trips). With no pattern established, limb (b)'s FULL_REFUND uplift and limb (c)'s conduct referral are both unavailable, and this trip's own already-non-material trace cannot be leveraged into a harsher remedy.

The $5.50 of ERP the rider highlights is the two off-route CTE gantries — $3.00 at CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) and $2.50 at CTE (Chin Swee Rd tunnel, towards City) — both flagged on_optimal_route false, with the optimal route carrying zero ERP. Under POL-RD-09(1) that ERP is ALREADY COMPREHENDED in the POL-RD-02 refund, because the recomputed fare credits only gantries lying on the optimal route (here none). It must never be added on top of the distance-and-time refund, so the rider's framing of '$26.04 including $5.50 of ERP' cannot be counted twice; the anti-double-count rule fixes the exposure at the single recomputed figure.

The arithmetic yields a PARTIAL_REFUND, not a full one. charged_total is 26.04; the recomputed optimal-route fare is (3.80 + 0.75 x 7.2 + 0.28 x 19.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 15.32, with no on-optimal-route ERP, no fixed surcharge, no waiting fee and no promo. The refund is 26.04 - 15.32 = 10.72, rounded up to 10.75. That is 41.2% of charged_total — well short of the 90% of charged_total that POL-RD-02 requires before a FULL_REFUND issues — so the contested $26.04 cannot be returned in full. The rider was billed 10.8 km against a 10.78 km trace, so there is likewise no unbilled-distance shortfall to support any DRIVER_COMPENSATION under POL-RD-04, and the amount moving is confined to the partial refund.

The rider cannot extract an additional billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4). Both charged gantries are matched to the trace: the nearest fix to CTE (Braddell Rd) is 0.0 m and the nearest fix to CTE (Chin Swee Rd tunnel) is 24.1 m, both well inside the 250 m crossing radius, so neither line is a gantry the vehicle never passed and neither is a phantom. Nor is any airport surcharge present (airport_surcharge is 0.0 on a Toa Payoh-to-Bugis trip). No standalone correction is therefore due on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: this is a route-deviation case on the Toa Payoh Central to Bugis Junction trip of 17 July 2026 (TRP-00106).

Finding on the route. The governing GPS trace (EV-GPS-00106) measures 10.78 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 7.2 km (EV-TRIP-00106). POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern, and it forbids citing the trip record's rounded 10.8 km convenience copy for the threshold test; measured the way the clause requires, the excess is 3.58 km, or 49.72% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km absolute), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. The same figure sits just below the 50%-of-optimal and 8.0 km lines that would make the deviation additionally MATERIAL, so no material-deviation finding is recorded. I do not treat the trace as impaired: it carries 169 fixes at a 10-second interval with 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, nowhere near the POL-RD-07 thresholds. Both advocates' readings of this arithmetic are accepted.

No exoneration. Nothing excuses the excess. There is no traffic advisory that can exonerate under POL-RD-03: EV-ADVIS-00106-01 is present but empty, so it names no road and asserts no closure, and its absence is itself citable. The single in-app message (EV-CHAT-00106, sent 08:46:30) is a complaint, not an instruction; it carries no waypoint hint and names no road, so the POL-RD-04 corroboration test cannot be run, the clause is unavailable, and no distance is excluded from excess. There was no amended pickup or dropoff (POL-RD-05 is not engaged) and this is not a pooled trip (POL-RD-12 is not engaged; vehicle_type is RYDE_TAXI).

Refund. The fare is METERED and no exoneration applies, so POL-RD-02 fixes the outcome arithmetically, not by discretion: charged_total is 26.04; the recomputed optimal-route fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 7.2 + 0.28 x 19.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP on the optimal route + no fixed surcharge, no waiting fee, no promo = 15.32. The refund is 26.04 - 15.32 = 10.72, rounded up to SGD 10.75. That is 41.2% of the charged total, well under the 90% that would make it a FULL_REFUND, and well above the 0.50 de minimis floor, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND.

ERP. The 5.50 of ERP (3.00 at CTE Braddell Rd and 2.50 at the CTE Chin Swee tunnel, both off the optimal route) is already comprehended inside the 10.75, because the recomputed fare credits only gantries lying on the optimal route and the optimal route carries none. It is itemised here for transparency and must not be added on top, per POL-RD-09(1). Both gantries are matched to the trace (nearest fixes 0.0 m and 24.1 m, inside the 250 m radius) and airport_surcharge is 0.0 on a non-airport trip, so no separate billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) arises.

Driver compensation. There is no unbilled-distance shortfall: the fare_breakdown charged 10.8 km against a 10.78 km trace, so POL-RD-04's compensation limb is not triggered and no payment to the driver is due.

Escalation and referrals. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing or non-covering artifact; the refund is far below the 150.00 ceiling; and every charge line has a counterpart. No POL-RD-06 repeat pattern exists (0 deviation flags across 96 completed trips), so there is no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral. No POL-RD-09(4) referral arises. The referrals list is therefore empty.

Outcome. The rider's claim of a genuine detour is supported, but the contest is a partial one: SGD 10.75 of the 26.04 charged is returned to the rider as a PARTIAL_REFUND.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
